# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | blue | yellow | red |
| 7 | red | blue | yellow |
| 8 | yellow | red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to transmit the manual to Deaf using only visible gestures. I will use a fixed gesture code: 👍=blue, 👌=green, ✋=yellow, 🤟=red. Each row is sent as the display number followed by outputs for light blue, green, and yellow; 🤝 separates rows. Display numbers are represented by repeated ☝ gestures.

```code
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👌", "✋", "🤟", "👏"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "👍", "✋", "🤟", "🤝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "🤟", "👍", "✋", "🤝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "✋", "🤟", "👍"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | blue | yellow | red |
| 7 | red | blue | yellow |
| 8 | yellow | red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please send me the manual's complete rule and tell me exactly what visual facts Deaf must report. Also establish with Deaf a protocol for reporting wire positions and markings using gestures.
Deaf says: The bomb display reads 8. The light is green. The wires, in order, are wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, and wire 3 blue.

The blind monkey cannot see gestures, so I must pass everything through Deaf. I will reinforce the color code, give the complete lookup table in a fixed positional format, and then provide the bomb report: display 8, green light, and wires 1–3 red/yellow/blue. Deaf should verbally relay these facts and the rule to Blind.

```code
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👌", "✋", "🤟", "👏"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "👍", "✋", "🤟", "🤝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "🤟", "👍", "✋", "🤝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "✋", "🤟", "👍", "👏"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "👌", "🤟", "✋", "👍"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | blue | yellow | red |
| 7 | red | blue | yellow |
| 8 | yellow | red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I have received: display 8, light green, wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 blue. What does the manual say to cut for this combination?

The manual maps display 8 with a green light to red. Therefore Blind must cut the red wire, which is wire 1. I will signal Deaf using the established color code, with one ☝ indicating wire position 1 followed by 🤟 for red.

```code
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "🤟"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | blue | yellow | red |
| 7 | red | blue | yellow |
| 8 | yellow | red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf relayed five gesture sequences: (1) one pointing-up hand, thumbs up, OK hand, raised open palm, love-you hand, clapping hands; (2) four pointing-up hands, thumbs up, raised open palm, love-you hand, handshake; (3) seven pointing-up hands, love-you hand, thumbs up, raised open palm, handshake; (4) eight pointing-up hands, raised open palm, love-you hand, thumbs up, clapping hands; (5) eight pointing-up hands, OK hand, love-you hand, raised open palm, thumbs up. Please translate these into the manual's exact rule and tell me which wire to cut.

The five sequences encode the color mapping and the three manual rows. For display 8 with green light, the manual gives red. Since wire 1 is red, Blind must cut wire 1. I will send Deaf a clear report code: display 8, input light green, required color red, separator, then wire position 1 and its red marking.

```code
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "👌", "🤟", "👏", "☝", "🤟"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | blue | yellow | red |
| 7 | red | blue | yellow |
| 8 | yellow | red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please answer in plain speech: for display 8, green light, and wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue, which exact wire position must I cut? If you cannot state it directly, explain the gesture code first.

I cannot speak directly, but Deaf can see my gesture and tell Blind in plain speech. The manual gives red for display 8 with a green light, and the red wire is wire 1. I will therefore signal the established code for position 1 followed by red.

```code
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "🤟"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | blue | yellow | red |
| 7 | red | blue | yellow |
| 8 | yellow | red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please answer the bomb decision directly with exactly one gesture: thumbs up means cut wire 1, victory hand means cut wire 2, love-you hand means cut wire 3. Do not send the longer encoded message.
Blind gestures to Mute: [👍 ✌ 🤟]

The manual requires red for display 8 with green light, and red is wire 1. I cannot gesture directly to Blind; my gesture reaches Deaf, who can report it aloud. I will send exactly the requested single gesture for wire 1.

```code
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | blue | yellow | red |
| 7 | red | blue | yellow |
| 8 | yellow | red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Your last message had two gestures and is ambiguous. Send exactly one gesture only: thumbs up means wire 1, victory hand means wire 2, love-you hand means wire 3. No other gesture or sequence.

The required cut remains wire 1: display 8 with green light maps to red, and wire 1 is red. I will send Deaf exactly the agreed single gesture for wire 1, so Deaf can state it to Blind.

```code
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```
